milts: milts — mercy, kindness, favor (feminine, nominative singular; cf. 'mild')
morgẹnlongne: morgenlang — lasting all morning, morning-long (adjective, accusative singular masculine, agreeing with dæg; the dot under ẹ is Klaeber's sign that the vowel does not count in the metre)

sārigmōdum: sārigmōd — sore-minded, grieving (adjective used as a noun, dative plural masculine; sārig 'sore' + mōd 'mind')
te: te — to (the manuscript's spelling of tō, which most editors print; preposition with the dative, after wēnan 'expect from'; see tō)

ungyfeðe: ungīefeðe — not granted, ungiven (adjective, nominative singular feminine, agreeing with milts; un- + gīefeðe 'granted'; uncertain, the metre is irregular)

weorðeð: weorðan — comes to be, becomes, happens (3rd singular present, strong verb III, -eð for -eþ; cf. 'worth' in 'woe worth the day')
wilgeofa: wilgeofa — wish-giver, giver of what is desired (weak masculine, nominative singular; wil 'wish' + giefa 'giver'; a title of a generous lord)
wælreste: wælrest — slaughter-rest, bed of the slain (feminine, dative singular, of place; wæl 'slaughter' + rest 'resting-place')
wēnum: wēn — hope, expectation, doubt (feminine, dative plural, after on: 'in expectation'; cf. 'ween')
wērge: wērig — weary, worn out (adjective, strong accusative singular feminine, agreeing with lāfe; cf. 'weary')
ābrēot: ābrēotan — cut down, destroy, kill (3rd singular preterite, strong verb II; Klaeber's ābrēot, where others read ābrēat)
āgeaf: āgiefan — gave, gave back, delivered (3rd singular preterite, strong verb V; ondslyht āgeaf 'gave a blow in return')
āhredde: āhreddan — rescued, set free (3rd singular preterite, weak verb; Bugge's emendation of the manuscript's bryda heorde)
ōhtheres: Ōhthere — Ohthere, son of Ongentheow and brother of Onela, a Swedish prince (genitive singular, dependent on fæder and on mōdor)
